seo_title: Deputy vs Tanda: Australian Payroll & Rostering Audit (2026)
meta_description: Technical comparison of Deputy and Tanda for Australian Fair Work compliance, Xero integration, and workforce management architecture.
direct_verdict: Deputy is the superior choice for mid-market firms requiring deep API extensibility and global scalability. Tanda is the optimal choice for Australian-centric SMBs needing a unified, low-friction payroll and rostering stack.

comparison_matrix.product_a_spec: Deep API sync with multi-entity support
Robust REST API for custom integrations
Full month charge for any activity

product_a_pros: Superior API documentation for custom ERP/BI workflows
Advanced biometric kiosk prevents buddy punching
Granular location hierarchy and multi-entity management
product_a_cons: Aggressive billing policy charges full month for any user activity
Hidden SMS costs can escalate for high-turnover shift environments
product_b_pros: Lower per-user cost for all-in-one bundle
Eliminates third-party integration friction via native payroll
product_b_cons: Opaque pricing structure requires manual quote requests
Limited developer ecosystem compared to market competitors
hidden_gotchas: Deputy enforces a strict $30 AUD minimum monthly spend regardless of user count, which penalizes very small teams. Furthermore, Deputy's billing logic is punitive: archiving a user mid-month still triggers a full month's charge. Tanda's reliance on 'Request Pricing' models often masks implementation fees and setup costs that are not transparent until the contract stage, potentially leading to higher total cost of ownership than the advertised per-user rate.
